mechanism: Ketorolac (NSAID) reduces renal perfusion and increases chlorpromazine levels through decreased clearance, while chlorpromazine may increase NSAID gastric toxicity risk; both agents have CNS depressant effects.
action: Monitor renal function and for increased chlorpromazine adverse effects (sedation, orthostasis); consider alternative analgesia or use lowest effective ketorolac dose for shortest duration with gastroprotection.
